transcript:
This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
>> Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Amy Held.
Flights are slowly recovering from Friday's ground stop.
Data show most are taking off on time.
Still, cancellations and delays have topped 8,000 so far today.
Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy blames a contractor
updating old telecom equipment and Congress
for not giving the FAA more money.
Now he is asking for $50 billion.
NPR's Marlaison reports.
>> Right now, Republicans who are in charge of Congress
until January have already approved $12.5 billion
in that one big, beautiful bill for safety upgrades.
And ranking Democrats on the House Transportation
and Infrastructure Committee said that the administration
has only spent $1 billion of those funds.
>> That's NPR's Marlaison reporting.
The alleged Chinese spy linked to the former Nvidia head
is no longer with her company, Megaspede.
NPR's Ava Pukach has this report.
>> In a statement to NPR, Megaspede said Alice Wong,
who was an executive with the company,
officially left Megaspede effective August 30th of 2025
and currently has no role with the company.
The company says a quote does not comment
on Ms. Wong's personal and private matters.
The New York Times reported that U.S. intelligence officials
believe Alice Wong to be a Chinese spy.
NPR has not independently confirmed that reporting.
Jensen Wong stepped down from his role at Nvidia
following the New York Times reporting
on his extramarital affairs.
Megaspede is a major buyer of advanced chips from Nvidia.
Megaspede says it is reviewing the reporting
and will communicate further with its stakeholders
as appropriate.
Ava Pukach, NPR News.
>> A federal judge has temporarily blocked
President Trump's plans to redevelop a public park
and golf course in Washington, D.C.
NPR's Kate Bartlett reports.
>> The judge on Saturday ordered a two-week delay
to any work on the site,
which had been due to close on Sunday for 15 months
while it was redeveloped.
Trump, an avid golfer, wants to turn the historic site,
East Potomac Golf Links,
into a championship-level golf course.
The plaintiffs in the case,
including the D.C. Preservation League,
argue the new course would be unaffordable.
On Saturday, before the order, Trump said on social media
that anyone in the D.C. area would be given a 50% discount.
Kate Bartlett, NPR News.
>> In Alaska's U.S. Senate race,
Democrat Mary Pultola now has 49.9% of the vote,
according to the latest AP tally.
Alaska allows absentee ballots to arrive 15 days
after Election Day -- that's Wednesday.
A candidate must hit the 50% threshold
to avoid the state's ranked-choice voting process.
Pultola's campaign said in a statement yesterday,
"There is no mathematical path
for the incumbent Republican Senator Dan Sullivan to win."
This is NPR News.
Holiday dinners and parties will be taking place
over the next two months, which means lots of food.
The Environmental Protection Agency
says the average American household
wastes nearly $3,000 a year on uneaten food.
Scott Massione from member station WYPR
reports on ways to cut down.
>> The U.S. wastes about 30% of the food supply,
and half of that comes from households,
according to Johns Hopkins environmental health researcher
Ronnie Neff.
But there are ways to get some of that back.
>> Use your freezer.
There's a lot of things that can be frozen
that, you know, most people don't recognize.
>> Ness says to remember to label those foods
and consider having a day for eating leftover meals each week
to ensure everything gets gobbled up.
Another way to reduce waste is using online food calculators
to make portions suitable for the number of guests at a party.
For NPR News, I'm Scott Massione in Baltimore.
>> The Rock and Roll Hall of Fame inducted a new class
comprising 18 musicians.
Among those paid tribute, Phil Collins.
Collins is part of an esteemed group
to have been inducted more than once his first time
with his old band, Genesis, in 2010.
Last night in Los Angeles, he was given a standing ovation.
>> Such an outpouring of emotion.
I had tears in my eyes, I'm going to be honest.
>> Also inducted Oasis, Queen Latifah, and Iron Maiden.
Artists only become eligible 25 years
after their first release.
Aerosmith and RunDMC gave a surprise closer
with a rendition of "Walk This Way."
This is NPR News.

topics.text: FAA recovers from Friday ground stop; 8,000 cancellations and delays so far today
Transportation Secretary Duffy asks Congress for $50 billion to fund FAA upgrades
Alleged Chinese spy linked to Nvidia's Jensen Huang's affair leaves Megaspede, company says
Federal judge temporarily blocks Trump's East Potomac Golf Links redevelopment in Washington, D.C.
Democrat Mary Peltola nears 50% in Alaska Senate race, avoiding ranked-choice voting
EPA says average American household wastes nearly $3,000 a year in uneaten food
Rock and Roll Hall of Fame inducts 18 musicians, including Phil Collins, Oasis, and Iron Maiden
